newsitem.title: USA: U.S. high court orders religion bankruptcy review.
newsitem.headline: U.S. high court orders religion bankruptcy review.

text.p: The Supreme Court Friday ordered further review in a case involving efforts on behalf of creditors to recover money a couple donated to their church before they went bankrupt.

The justices granted an appeal by a bankruptcy trustee who seeks to recoup contributions made when the Minnesota couple claimed to be insolvent in the year before their bankruptcy filing. At issue was $13,450 that Bruce and Nancy Young gave to the Crystal Evangelical Church in New Hope, Minnesota, before their electrical contracting business failed.
A federal judge upheld the trustee's claim that the money should be returned. The case then went to a U.S. appeals court, which asked the Justice Department for its views.

On President Clinton's orders, the department took the unusual step of switching its position, dropping its support for the trustee and siding with the church. The case involved whether efforts to recoup the money violated the guarantee of freedom of religion under the First Amendment to the Constitution or discriminated against religion under the 1993 Religious Freedom Restoration law.

The appeals court, by 2-1, ruled for the church. It said allowing debtors a fresh start and protecting interests of creditors lacked the compelling government interest required under the 1993 law for the trustee to claim the money.

The Supreme Court, in a brief order, set aside the appeals court's decision and sent the case back to the appeals court for further consideration in view of this week's high court decision that struck down the 1993 law as unconstitutional.
Attorneys for the church had argued the trustee could not recover money given before the filing of bankruptcy when there was no evidence of intent to hinder or defraud creditors.
